q: The memorandum of charges for imposition of a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is issued in Standard Form:

options.A: SF-1
options.B: SF-5
options.C: SF-7
options.D: SF-11

e: The memorandum of charges for imposition of a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is issued in Standard Form SF-5.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Censure is a minor penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.
2. Compulsory retirement is a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: censure is a minor penalty, while compulsory retirement is a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.

q: The monthly wage ceiling for eligibility for Productivity Linked Bonus (PLB) on the Railways is:
e: The monthly wage ceiling for eligibility for Productivity Linked Bonus on the Railways is Rs 7,000; staff drawing wages above this ceiling are not eligible.

q: Overtime allowance for hours of duty performed beyond the rostered hours is ordinarily payable at:

options.A: The ordinary rate of pay
options.B: One and a half times the ordinary rate of pay
options.C: Two and a half times the ordinary rate of pay
options.D: Twice (double) the ordinary rate of pay

e: Overtime allowance for hours of duty performed beyond the rostered hours is ordinarily payable at twice, i.e., double, the ordinary rate of pay.

q: For the purpose of Night Duty Allowance, 'night duty' means duty performed between:

options.A: 20:00 hrs and 05:00 hrs
options.B: 21:00 hrs and 06:00 hrs
options.C: 22:00 hrs and 06:00 hrs
options.D: 23:00 hrs and 07:00 hrs

e: For the purpose of Night Duty Allowance, 'night duty' means duty performed between 22:00 hrs and 06:00 hrs.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for more than 6 hours but less than 12 hours in a day. Daily Allowance is admissible to him at:

options.A: 30% of the admissible rate
options.B: 70% of the admissible rate
options.C: 50% of the admissible rate
options.D: The full admissible rate

e: Where absence from headquarters on tour is more than 6 hours but less than 12 hours in a day, Daily Allowance is admissible at 70% of the admissible rate.

q: Where a transfer of a railway servant does not involve a change of residence (for example, transfer within the same station or to a station within 20 km), Composite Transfer Grant is admissible at:

options.A: 33% of the last month's basic pay
options.B: 80% of the last month's basic pay
options.C: 50% of the last month's basic pay
options.D: No Composite Transfer Grant is admissible in such cases

e: Where a transfer does not involve a change of residence, such as a transfer within the same station or to a nearby station, Composite Transfer Grant is admissible at 33% of the last month's basic pay.

q: Appointment on compassionate grounds on the Railways is intended to:

options.A: Provide employment to a dependent of every railway servant on his retirement
options.B: Guarantee employment to the ward of a railway servant as a matter of right
options.C: Compensate the family of a deceased railway servant by way of enhanced pension
options.D: Enable the family of a railway servant who dies in harness, or who is retired on medical grounds, to tide over the sudden financial crisis, where the family is left in indigent circumstances

e: Appointment on compassionate grounds enables the family of a railway servant who dies in harness, or is retired on medical grounds, to tide over the sudden financial crisis, where the family is left in indigent circumstances; it is not a matter of right.

q: The inter-se seniority of direct recruits appointed to a grade is determined by:

options.A: Their respective ages on the date of appointment
options.B: The dates on which they actually join duty
options.C: The order of merit assigned to them in the select list at the time of selection
options.D: The alphabetical order of their names in the panel

e: The inter-se seniority of direct recruits appointed to a grade is determined by the order of merit assigned to them in the select list at the time of selection, not by their dates of joining.

q: Service rendered by a railway servant on an ad hoc (fortuitous) basis before his regular appointment to a grade:

options.A: Does not count towards seniority in that grade
options.B: Counts in full towards seniority in that grade
options.C: Counts to the extent of one-half towards seniority
options.D: Counts towards seniority only if it exceeds one year

e: Service rendered on an ad hoc or fortuitous basis before regular appointment to a grade does not count towards seniority in that grade.

q: Where two or more direct recruits are bracketed at the same position in the order of merit, their inter-se seniority is decided by:

options.A: Length of service rendered in any previous post
options.B: Higher educational qualification
options.C: Earlier date of submission of application
options.D: Date of birth, the older candidate ranking senior

e: Where two or more direct recruits are bracketed at the same position in the order of merit, their inter-se seniority is decided by date of birth, the older candidate ranking senior.

q: Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in direct recruitment on the Railways is, respectively:
e: Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in direct recruitment on the Railways is 15%, 7.5% and 27% respectively.

q: Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), other than the classes covered under the existing reservations, in direct recruitment is:
e: Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections, other than the classes already covered under the existing reservations, in direct recruitment is 10%.

q: Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes on the Railways is operated through:

options.A: Vacancy-based rosters, applied to the vacancies arising in a year
options.B: Seniority lists maintained for each category
options.C: Post-based rosters, the roster points being applied to the posts in a cadre
options.D: Waiting lists prepared by the Railway Recruitment Boards

e: Reservation on the Railways is operated through post-based rosters, in which the roster points are applied to the posts in a cadre, rather than through vacancy-based rosters.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Hours of Employment Regulations (HOER):
1. Staff classified as 'Intensive' are rostered to work 42 hours per week.
2. Staff classified as 'Essentially Intermittent' are rostered to work 54 hours per week.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: under HOER, staff classified as 'Intensive' are rostered to work 42 hours per week, and staff classified as 'Essentially Intermittent' are rostered to work 54 hours per week.

q: A railway servant who is medically decategorised, i.e., declared unfit for the post held by him but fit for other duties, is:

options.A: Absorbed, as far as possible, in an alternative post carrying the same scale of pay and status, and his pay is protected
options.B: Retired from service immediately, without offer of alternative employment
options.C: Absorbed only in a post carrying a lower scale of pay
options.D: Kept on half pay till he attains the age of superannuation

e: A railway servant who is medically decategorised, i.e., declared unfit for the post held but fit for other duties, is absorbed as far as possible in an alternative post carrying the same scale of pay and status, and his pay is protected.

q: In the medical classification of railway servants, 'Aye-One' (A-1) denotes:

options.A: The category prescribing the lowest standard of vision
options.B: The category applicable only to ministerial staff in offices
options.C: A category which has since been abolished on the Railways
options.D: The highest medical fitness category, prescribed for staff whose duties are directly connected with the running of trains and require the strictest standards of physical fitness and vision

e: 'Aye-One' (A-1) is the highest medical fitness category, prescribed for staff whose duties are directly connected with the running of trains and require the strictest standards of physical fitness and vision.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Periodical Medical Examination (PME) of staff in the 'Aye' medical categories:
1. Such staff undergo PME every four years up to the age of 45 years.
2. Between the ages of 45 and 55 years, PME is held every two years, and annually thereafter.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: staff in the 'Aye' medical categories undergo Periodical Medical Examination every four years up to the age of 45 years, every two years between 45 and 55 years, and annually thereafter.

q: A railway servant who is declared by the competent medical authority to be completely and permanently incapacitated for further service of any kind on the Railways is:

options.A: Granted study leave for the remaining period of service
options.B: Retired from service on invalidation
options.C: Granted Extra Ordinary Leave for a period of five years
options.D: Retained permanently against a supernumerary post

e: A railway servant declared by the competent medical authority to be completely and permanently incapacitated for further service of any kind on the Railways is retired from service on invalidation.

q: Study leave granted to a railway servant:

options.A: Counts as qualifying service for pension and does not postpone his date of increment
options.B: Does not count as qualifying service for pension
options.C: Postpones his next increment by the period of the leave
options.D: Is treated in the same manner as Extra Ordinary Leave for all purposes

e: Study leave granted to a railway servant counts as qualifying service for pension and does not postpone his date of increment.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the rates of Transport Allowance payable to a railway servant are prescribed with reference to:

options.A: The pay level of the employee alone
options.B: The pay level of the employee and the classification of the city in which he is posted
options.C: The distance between his residence and his office
options.D: The length of his service in the Railways

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the rates of Transport Allowance are prescribed with reference to the pay level of the employee and the classification of the city in which he is posted.

q: Transport Allowance is admissible at double the normal rate to:

options.A: Blind and orthopaedically handicapped (Divyangjan) railway servants
options.B: Railway servants posted in metropolitan cities
options.C: Running staff performing kilometreage duties
options.D: Railway servants residing beyond 10 km from their office

e: Transport Allowance is admissible at double the normal rate to blind and orthopaedically handicapped (Divyangjan) railway servants, in recognition of their additional commuting hardship.

q: Transport Allowance is NOT admissible to a railway servant who:

options.A: Is on casual leave for a few days in a month
options.B: Is transferred in public interest from one station to another
options.C: Resides within the same city in which his office is located
options.D: Is provided with a staff car or official transport facility for commuting between his residence and office

e: Transport Allowance is not admissible to a railway servant who is provided with a staff car or official transport facility for commuting between his residence and office, since the facility serves the very purpose of the allowance.

q: The Special Allowance for Child Care admissible to a woman railway servant with disability is payable:

options.A: In respect of all her children till they attain the age of 18 years
options.B: In respect of her two eldest surviving children till they attain the age of five years
options.C: In respect of her two eldest surviving children, from their birth till they attain the age of two years
options.D: In respect of only one child, till the child attains the age of one year

e: The Special Allowance for Child Care admissible to a woman railway servant with disability is payable in respect of her two eldest surviving children, from their birth till they attain the age of two years.

q: The Risk and Hardship Matrix introduced on the recommendations of the 7th CPC is meant to:

options.A: Classify cities for the purpose of House Rent Allowance
options.B: Grade the various risk and hardship allowances into cells according to the level of risk and hardship involved in the duties
options.C: Determine the rate of Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants
options.D: Fix the rates of Transport Allowance for different cities

e: The Risk and Hardship Matrix introduced on the recommendations of the 7th CPC grades the various risk and hardship allowances into cells according to the level of risk and hardship involved in the duties.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Home Town Leave Travel Concession is admissible to a railway servant once in a block of two years.
2. 'Anywhere in India' Leave Travel Concession is admissible once in a block of four years, in lieu of one Home Town LTC entitlement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Home Town Leave Travel Concession is admissible once in a block of two years, and 'Anywhere in India' LTC is admissible once in a block of four years, in lieu of one Home Town LTC entitlement.

q: A railway servant who could not avail the Leave Travel Concession of a particular block during the block period itself may avail it:

options.A: In the first year of the succeeding block, as a grace period
options.B: At any time during the next two blocks
options.C: Only at the time of his retirement
options.D: In no case, as it lapses absolutely at the end of the block

e: A railway servant who could not avail the Leave Travel Concession of a particular block during the block period itself may avail it in the first year of the succeeding block, as a grace period.

q: The maximum amount of Personal Computer Advance admissible to a railway servant is:

options.B: Rs 50,000 or the actual price of the personal computer, whichever is less

e: The maximum amount of Personal Computer Advance admissible to a railway servant is Rs 50,000 or the actual price of the personal computer, whichever is less.

q: The Flood Advance granted to railway servants affected by floods or other natural calamities is:

options.A: An advance bearing interest at the rate applicable to Provident Fund
options.B: A free grant which is not required to be recovered
options.C: An interest-free advance, recoverable in monthly instalments
options.D: An advance recoverable only from the gratuity of the railway servant

e: The Flood Advance granted to railway servants affected by floods or other natural calamities is an interest-free advance, recoverable in monthly instalments.

q: Which of the following is NOT an activity financed from the Staff Benefit Fund?

options.A: Scholarships for the higher education of the children of railway servants
options.B: Promotion of sports, recreation and cultural activities among staff
options.C: Maintenance of holiday homes and relief to staff in distress
options.D: Grant of house building loans to railway servants

e: House building loans are granted as House Building Advance under separate rules and are not financed from the Staff Benefit Fund, which funds only staff welfare activities such as scholarships, sports, recreation, holiday homes and relief in distress.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. All fines realised from railway servants are credited to the Staff Benefit Fund.
2. The Staff Benefit Fund receives an annual per capita contribution from Railway revenues.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: all fines realised from railway servants are credited to the Staff Benefit Fund, and the Fund also receives an annual per capita contribution from Railway revenues.

q: Family pension at the enhanced rate is payable at:

options.A: 50% of the last pay drawn by the deceased railway servant
options.B: 30% of the last pay drawn by the deceased railway servant
options.C: 40% of the last pay drawn by the deceased railway servant
options.D: 60% of the last pay drawn by the deceased railway servant

e: Family pension at the enhanced rate is payable at 50% of the last pay drawn by the deceased railway servant, as against the normal rate of 30%.

q: Family pension is ordinarily payable to a son of a deceased railway servant until he:

options.A: Attains the age of 18 years
options.B: Attains the age of 25 years, gets married, or starts earning his livelihood, whichever is the earliest
options.C: Attains the age of 21 years, whether or not he is earning
options.D: Attains the age of 30 years in all cases

e: Family pension is ordinarily payable to a son until he attains the age of 25 years, gets married, or starts earning his livelihood, whichever is the earliest.

q: Family pension is payable to an unmarried, widowed or divorced daughter of a deceased railway servant:

options.A: Only up to the age of 25 years
options.B: Only up to the age of 21 years
options.C: Only if she was below 25 years of age at the time of the death of the railway servant
options.D: Even beyond the age of 25 years, until she gets married or remarried, or starts earning her livelihood

e: An unmarried, widowed or divorced daughter remains eligible for family pension even beyond the age of 25 years, until she gets married or remarried, or starts earning her livelihood.

q: Family pension payable to a son or daughter of a deceased railway servant who is suffering from a disorder or disability of mind or is physically disabled so as to be unable to earn a livelihood is admissible:

options.A: For his or her lifetime, even beyond the age of 25 years
options.B: Only up to the age of 25 years
options.C: Only up to the age of 21 years
options.D: Only up to the age of 18 years

e: Family pension payable to a son or daughter suffering from a disorder or disability of mind, or physically disabled so as to be unable to earn a livelihood, is admissible for his or her lifetime, even beyond 25 years.

q: A railway servant who retires from service with less than 10 years of qualifying service is entitled to:

options.A: Full pension proportionate to his short service
options.B: Only a refund of his own Provident Fund subscription
options.C: Service gratuity at the rate of half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, in lieu of pension
options.D: No retirement benefit of any kind

e: A railway servant retiring with less than 10 years of qualifying service is not entitled to pension, but gets service gratuity at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, in lieu of pension.

q: Pro-rata pension is sanctioned to a railway servant when he:

options.A: Is sent on deputation to another office for a fixed tenure
options.B: Is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking or an autonomous body, proportionate to the qualifying service rendered by him under the Railways
options.C: Seeks voluntary retirement before completing 25 years of service
options.D: Is transferred from one Railway to another

e: Pro-rata pension is sanctioned to a railway servant when he is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking or an autonomous body, proportionate to the qualifying service rendered by him under the Railways.

q: Where departmental or judicial proceedings are pending against a railway servant at the time of his retirement, the correct position is that:

options.A: Full pension and full gratuity are paid to him immediately
options.B: No pension is paid to him, but the gratuity is paid in full
options.C: The gratuity is paid, but the pension is stopped altogether
options.D: Only provisional pension is sanctioned to him, and the gratuity is withheld until the conclusion of the proceedings

e: Where departmental or judicial proceedings are pending at the time of retirement, only provisional pension is sanctioned to the railway servant and the gratuity is withheld until the conclusion of the proceedings.

q: The effect of dismissal from service on the pensionary benefits of a railway servant is that:

options.A: His past service is forfeited and he is ordinarily not entitled to any pension or gratuity
options.B: His pension is reduced by one-half, but gratuity is paid in full
options.C: His full pension is protected, but gratuity is forfeited
options.D: Only his gratuity is forfeited, and pension is paid in full

e: Dismissal from service entails forfeiture of the railway servant's past service, and he is ordinarily not entitled to any pension or gratuity.

q: A compassionate allowance, sanctioned to a railway servant who is dismissed or removed from service but is considered deserving of special consideration, shall not exceed:

options.A: One-half of the pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him
options.B: Two-thirds of the pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him had he retired on a compensation pension
options.C: Three-fourths of the pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him
options.D: The full pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him

e: A compassionate allowance sanctioned to a dismissed or removed railway servant deserving special consideration shall not exceed two-thirds of the pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him had he retired on a compensation pension.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Future good conduct is an implied condition of every grant of pension to a railway servant.
2. The competent authority may withhold or withdraw a pension, in whole or in part, if the pensioner is convicted of a serious crime or is found guilty of grave misconduct.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: future good conduct is an implied condition of every grant of pension, and the competent authority may withhold or withdraw a pension, in whole or in part, if the pensioner is convicted of a serious crime or found guilty of grave misconduct.

q: A railway servant who retires on superannuation and applies for commutation of a portion of his pension within one year of the date of his retirement:

options.A: Is not required to undergo a medical examination for the purpose of commutation
options.B: Must invariably undergo a medical examination before commutation is allowed
options.C: Is not permitted to commute any portion of his pension within one year of retirement
options.D: Can commute his pension only after a medical examination by a Medical Board of the Railway Board

e: A railway servant retiring on superannuation who applies for commutation of a portion of his pension within one year of the date of retirement is not required to undergo a medical examination for the purpose.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing three years of qualifying service. The death gratuity payable to his family is:

options.A: 2 times his emoluments
options.B: 6 times his emoluments
options.C: 12 times his emoluments
options.D: 16½ times his emoluments

e: Death gratuity slabs: service of 3 years falls in the slab of 1 year or more but less than 5 years, for which gratuity is 6 times the emoluments (2 times below 1 year; 12 times for 5 to 20 years).

q: Which of the following is NOT a permissible purpose for making a final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund by a railway servant?

options.A: Meeting expenditure on the marriage of his son or daughter
options.B: Meeting expenditure on the higher education of his children
options.C: Purchasing a dwelling house or a site for a dwelling house
options.D: Undertaking a pleasure trip abroad

e: Final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund is permitted for specified purposes like marriage, higher education and purchase of a house or site; a pleasure trip abroad is not among the permissible purposes.

q: Which of the following statements about the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme is correct?

options.A: The employee is required to pay a monthly premium for the insurance cover
options.B: A fixed sum of Rs 10,000 is payable on the death of the member in all cases
options.C: An assurance benefit, linked to the balance in the member's Provident Fund account, is payable to the nominee on the death of the member while in service, without any contribution by the employee
options.D: The scheme covers the medical expenses of the family of the member

e: Under the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, an assurance benefit linked to the balance in the member's Provident Fund account is payable to the nominee on the death of the member while in service, without any contribution by the employee.

q: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEGIS), the monthly subscription of a member is apportioned between the Insurance Fund and the Savings Fund in the proportion of:

options.A: 50% to the Insurance Fund and 50% to the Savings Fund
options.B: 30% to the Insurance Fund and 70% to the Savings Fund
options.C: 70% to the Insurance Fund and 30% to the Savings Fund
options.D: 25% to the Insurance Fund and 75% to the Savings Fund

e: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the monthly subscription of a member is apportioned between the Insurance Fund and the Savings Fund in the proportion of 30% and 70% respectively.

q: On the implementation of the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission, the pay of serving railway servants was fixed by multiplying their pre-revised pay by a fitment factor of:
e: On implementation of the 7th CPC recommendations, the pay of serving railway servants was fixed by multiplying their pre-revised pay by a fitment factor of 2.57 and placing it in the pay matrix.

q: In the pay matrix introduced under the 7th CPC, the minimum pay at Level 1, which is the entry level, is:
e: In the pay matrix introduced under the 7th CPC, the minimum pay at Level 1, which is the entry level, is Rs 18,000.

q:
Consider the following statements about the pay matrix under the 7th CPC:
1. The pay matrix has replaced the earlier system of running pay bands and grade pays with a matrix of levels corresponding to the functional hierarchy.
2. Progression within a level is vertical, through annual increments, while movement on promotion or financial upgradation is to a higher level.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the pay matrix has replaced running pay bands and grade pays with levels corresponding to the functional hierarchy; progression within a level is vertical through annual increments, while promotion or financial upgradation takes the employee to a higher level.

q: As originally fixed on the implementation of the 7th CPC recommendations, when Dearness Allowance was below 25%, House Rent Allowance in X, Y and Z class cities was payable respectively at:

options.A: 30%, 20% and 10% of basic pay
options.B: 24%, 16% and 8% of basic pay
options.C: 27%, 18% and 9% of basic pay
options.D: 25%, 15% and 10% of basic pay

e: As originally fixed on implementation of the 7th CPC, when Dearness Allowance was below 25%, House Rent Allowance in X, Y and Z class cities was payable at 24%, 16% and 8% of basic pay respectively.

q: When Dearness Allowance crosses 50%, the rates of House Rent Allowance in X, Y and Z class cities stand revised respectively to:

options.A: 24%, 16% and 8% of basic pay
options.B: 27%, 18% and 9% of basic pay
options.C: 30%, 20% and 10% of basic pay
options.D: 32%, 22% and 12% of basic pay

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, HRA rates are linked to DA: when DA crosses 50%, the HRA for X, Y and Z class cities is revised upward to 30%, 20% and 10% of basic pay respectively.

q: For the purpose of House Rent Allowance, a city is classified as 'X' class if its population is:

options.A: 50 lakh and above
options.B: 25 lakh and above
options.C: 10 lakh and above
options.D: 1 crore and above

e: For HRA purposes, cities are classified by population under the 7th CPC, and an 'X' class city is one with a population of 50 lakh and above.

q: For the computation of Night Duty Allowance, night duty performed between 22:00 hours and 06:00 hours is given a weightage of:

options.A: 5 minutes for every hour of night duty
options.B: 10 minutes for every hour of night duty
options.C: 20 minutes for every hour of night duty
options.D: 30 minutes for every hour of night duty

e: For computing Night Duty Allowance, night duty performed between 22:00 and 06:00 hours is given a weightage of 10 minutes for every hour of night duty.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, staff classified as 'Continuous' are entitled to a period of rest in a week of not less than:

options.A: 24 consecutive hours
options.B: 30 consecutive hours, without any condition about the night
options.C: 36 consecutive hours including one full night
options.D: 30 consecutive hours including one full night

e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, staff classified as 'Continuous' must get a weekly rest of not less than 30 consecutive hours, including one full night.

q: Invalid pension is admissible to a railway servant who:

options.A: Retires on attaining the age of superannuation
options.B: Resigns from service to join another Government office
options.C: Is removed from service as a measure of penalty
options.D: Retires from service on being declared by the competent medical authority to be incapacitated, by bodily or mental infirmity, permanently for further service

e: Invalid pension is granted when a railway servant retires from service on being declared by the competent medical authority to be permanently incapacitated, by bodily or mental infirmity, for further service.

q: Extraordinary pension, including disability pension and extraordinary family pension, is admissible where:

options.A: The disablement or death of the railway servant is attributable to, or aggravated by, the conditions of his service, such as an injury sustained in the course of duty
options.B: The railway servant dies of an ordinary illness having no connection with his service
options.C: The railway servant retires voluntarily on completion of 20 years of service
options.D: The railway servant retires on superannuation in the normal course

e: Extraordinary pension is admissible where the disablement or death of the servant is attributable to, or aggravated by, the conditions of his service, such as an injury sustained in the course of duty.

q: Withholding of increments of pay with cumulative effect is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.A: A minor penalty
options.B: Not a penalty at all
options.C: A major penalty
options.D: A penalty only when imposed by the Railway Board

e: Withholding of increments with cumulative effect permanently affects the servant's future pay and pension, and is therefore classified as a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.

q: Recovery from the pay of a railway servant of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused by him to the Railways, by negligence or breach of orders, is:

options.A: A minor penalty
options.B: A major penalty
options.C: Not treated as a penalty
options.D: A criminal proceeding against the railway servant

e: Recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to the Railways by the servant's negligence or breach of orders is listed as a minor penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: For the imposition of a minor penalty on a railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: A full-fledged departmental inquiry must invariably be held before imposing the penalty
options.B: The railway servant need not be given any opportunity to represent against the proposed penalty
options.C: The penalty can be imposed only after an inquiry by the Union Public Service Commission
options.D: A formal departmental inquiry is not mandatory, and the penalty may be imposed after giving the railway servant an opportunity to make a representation and considering the same

e: For a minor penalty, a formal departmental inquiry is not mandatory; the penalty may be imposed after giving the railway servant an opportunity to make a representation and considering the representation so made.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant:

options.A: May freely engage in private tuition work for remuneration
options.B: Shall not engage, directly or indirectly, in any trade or business, or accept any employment outside his public duties, without the previous sanction of the competent authority
options.C: May contest an election to a State Legislature while remaining in service
options.D: May freely accept valuable gifts from contractors having official dealings with him

e: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not engage, directly or indirectly, in any trade or business, or accept any outside employment, without the previous sanction of the competent authority.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in connection with his own marriage or the marriage of his son or daughter, a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Invite his official colleagues to the marriage ceremony
options.B: Receive ordinary customary gifts from his relatives
options.C: Give or take, or abet the giving or taking of, dowry
options.D: Avail leave for the marriage

e: The Conduct Rules prohibit a railway servant from giving or taking, or abetting the giving or taking of, dowry in connection with his own marriage or the marriage of his son or daughter.

q: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, the information sought by an applicant is ordinarily required to be provided within:

options.A: 30 days of the receipt of the application
options.B: 15 days of the receipt of the application
options.C: 45 days of the receipt of the application
options.D: 60 days of the receipt of the application

e: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, the information sought is ordinarily required to be provided within 30 days of the receipt of the application.

q: During the period of foreign service of a railway servant, the pension contribution and the leave salary contribution in respect of him are payable by:

options.A: The Railway Administration in all cases
options.B: The railway servant himself from his own pocket
options.C: The Ministry of Railways from the general revenues
options.D: The borrowing authority, i.e., the foreign employer

e: During foreign service, the pension contribution and leave salary contribution in respect of the railway servant are payable by the borrowing authority, i.e., the foreign employer, and not by the Railway Administration.

q: Posts surrendered by a Railway or a unit, as a result of work studies or otherwise, are:

options.A: Treated as lapsed permanently and can never be revived
options.B: Transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Credited to the Vacancy Bank, from which they can be utilised for creation of posts or for redeployment purposes
options.D: Utilised only for works expenditure of the Railway

e: Posts surrendered by a Railway or unit as a result of work studies or otherwise are credited to the Vacancy Bank, from which they can be utilised for creation of posts or for redeployment.

q: A Privilege Ticket Order (PTO) issued to a railway servant entitles him and his family to undertake the journey on payment of:

options.A: No fare at all
options.B: Half of the public fare
options.C: 25% of the public fare
options.D: One-third of the public fare

e: A Privilege Ticket Order entitles the railway servant and his family to undertake the journey on payment of one-third of the public fare.

q: The number of days of casual leave admissible to a railway servant in a calendar year is:

options.A: 8 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 12 days
options.D: 15 days

e: A railway servant is admissible 8 days of casual leave in a calendar year.

q: A railway servant may avail restricted holidays in a calendar year up to:

options.A: 1 day
options.B: 2 days
options.C: 3 days
options.D: 4 days

e: A railway servant may avail restricted holidays up to a maximum of 2 days in a calendar year, chosen from the list of restricted holidays.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a railway servant for donating blood is:

options.A: Half a day
options.B: Two days
options.C: One day
options.D: Three days

e: Special Casual Leave of one day is admissible to a railway servant for donating blood, on the day of donation.

q: The leave salary admissible to a railway servant during a period of Leave on Average Pay is equal to:

options.A: Half of the pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave
options.B: The pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave, but without Dearness Allowance
options.C: A fixed amount equal to the minimum of the pay level
options.D: The pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave, together with the allowances admissible thereon

e: Leave salary during Leave on Average Pay is equal to the pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave, together with the allowances admissible thereon.

q: Where a railway servant has availed Extra Ordinary Leave, or a period treated as dies non, during a half-year, the advance credit of Leave on Average Pay for the succeeding half-year is reduced by:

options.A: One-fifth of such leave or period
options.B: One-tenth of such leave or period, subject to a maximum reduction of 15 days
options.C: One-fourth of such leave or period
options.D: The full period of such leave

e: Where Extra Ordinary Leave or a dies non period occurs in a half-year, the advance credit of Leave on Average Pay for the next half-year is reduced by one-tenth of such period, subject to a maximum reduction of 15 days.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Paternity leave is also admissible to a male railway servant with less than two surviving children on the valid adoption of a child below the age of one year.
2. Paternity leave is debited to the Leave on Average Pay account of the railway servant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: paternity leave is admissible on the valid adoption of a child below the age of one year. Statement 2 is wrong: paternity leave is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant on leave shall not take up any service or accept any employment elsewhere without the previous sanction of the authority which sanctioned the leave.
2. Leave of any kind can be granted to a railway servant who is under suspension.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a servant on leave cannot take up service or employment elsewhere without the previous sanction of the leave-sanctioning authority. Statement 2 is wrong: leave of any kind cannot be granted to a servant under suspension.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a female railway servant for undergoing tubectomy (sterilisation) operation is:

options.A: 6 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 20 days

e: Special Casual Leave of 14 days is admissible to a female railway servant for undergoing tubectomy (sterilisation) operation.

q: 'Personal pay' granted to a railway servant means:

options.A: An advance increment granted to all staff on completion of five years of service
options.B: Additional pay granted to save him from a loss of substantive pay in respect of a permanent post, or in consideration of exceptional merit or a special personal qualification
options.C: Pay granted in lieu of Dearness Allowance
options.D: Pay drawn by an employee in an officiating capacity

e: 'Personal pay' is additional pay granted to save a railway servant from a loss of substantive pay in respect of a permanent post, or in consideration of exceptional merit or a special personal qualification.

q: 'Presumptive pay' of a post means:

options.A: The pay a railway servant actually draws in a month
options.B: The minimum pay of the level in which the post is placed
options.C: The pay to which a railway servant would be entitled if he held the post substantively and did duty in it
options.D: The pay fixed provisionally pending regular fixation

e: 'Presumptive pay' of a post is the pay to which a railway servant would be entitled if he held the post substantively and did duty in it.

q: Non-Practising Allowance (NPA) under the 7th CPC dispensation is admissible to:

options.A: Running staff in lieu of kilometreage
options.B: Accounts staff working on computers
options.C: Staff working in hazardous workshops
options.D: Railway medical officers, in lieu of private practice

e: Non-Practising Allowance under the 7th CPC is admissible to railway medical officers, in lieu of the private practice from which they are debarred.

q: The Additional Post Allowance (APA) introduced under the 7th CPC dispensation has replaced the earlier:

options.A: Dual charge allowance
options.B: Overtime allowance
options.C: Night duty allowance
options.D: Compensatory city allowance

e: The Additional Post Allowance introduced under the 7th CPC dispensation has replaced the earlier dual charge allowance payable for holding additional charge of another post.

q: A railway servant is said to have a 'lien' on a post when he:

options.A: Is appointed to officiate in that post for a short period
options.B: Holds substantively a permanent post, including a tenure post, to which he has been appointed substantively
options.C: Is posted against a work-charged vacancy
options.D: Is kept under suspension from that post

e: A railway servant has a 'lien' on a post when he holds substantively a permanent post, including a tenure post, to which he has been appointed substantively.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant acquires a lien on a post only on being appointed to it in a substantive capacity.
2. The lien of a railway servant on a post stands terminated on his acquiring a lien on another permanent post.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a lien is acquired only on substantive appointment to a post, and it stands terminated once the servant acquires a lien on another permanent post.

q: The value of the commuted portion of pension is calculated with reference to the commutation table in force and the age of the pensioner reckoned as:

options.A: His age on the date of retirement
options.B: His age on the date of application for commutation
options.C: His age in completed years on the date of retirement
options.D: His age on his next birthday

e: The value of the commuted portion of pension is calculated with reference to the commutation table and the age of the pensioner reckoned on his next birthday.

q: Departmental proceedings can be instituted against a retired railway servant, with the sanction of the competent authority, only in respect of an event which took place not more than:

options.A: Four years before the institution of such proceedings
options.B: Two years before the institution of such proceedings
options.C: Six years before the institution of such proceedings
options.D: Ten years before the institution of such proceedings

e: Departmental proceedings against a retired railway servant can be instituted, with the sanction of the competent authority, only in respect of an event which took place not more than four years before such institution.

q: Dearness Relief admissible to railway pensioners and family pensioners is:

options.A: A fixed amount of Rs 1,000 per month for all pensioners
options.B: Granted at the same percentage rates as Dearness Allowance admissible to serving railway employees
options.C: Granted only to pensioners who have not commuted any portion of their pension
options.D: Merged with the basic pension after every Pay Commission

e: Dearness Relief to railway pensioners and family pensioners is granted at the same percentage rates as the Dearness Allowance admissible to serving railway employees.

q: Under the National Pension System, the Tier-II account of a subscriber is:

options.A: The mandatory pension account from which no withdrawal is permitted before the age of 60 years
options.B: An account meant only for the Government's co-contribution
options.C: A voluntary savings account, from which the subscriber can withdraw his savings at any time
options.D: An account opened only after retirement for investing the annuity amount

e: In the National Pension System, the Tier-II account is a voluntary savings account from which the subscriber can withdraw his savings at any time; the locked-in pension account is Tier-I.

q: Fixed Medical Allowance admissible to a railway pensioner who is not availing the outdoor treatment facility under the health scheme is, under the 7th CPC dispensation:

options.A: Rs 500 per month
options.B: Rs 750 per month
options.C: Rs 2,000 per month
options.D: Rs 1,000 per month

e: Fixed Medical Allowance, admissible to a railway pensioner not availing outdoor treatment facility under the health scheme, is Rs 1,000 per month under the 7th CPC dispensation.

q: For computing the pensionary benefits of running staff, the element of running allowance reckoned as pay is:

options.A: 55% of the basic pay
options.B: 30% of the basic pay
options.C: 25% of the basic pay
options.D: 40% of the basic pay

e: For computing the pensionary benefits of running staff, the element of running allowance reckoned as pay is 55% of the basic pay.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Joining the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme (RELHS) is optional for a retiring railway employee.
2. A railway pensioner who avails medical facilities under RELHS is simultaneously entitled to Fixed Medical Allowance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: joining the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme is optional for a retiring employee. Statement 2 is wrong: a pensioner availing RELHS facilities is not simultaneously entitled to Fixed Medical Allowance.

q: Where a charged railway servant does not plead guilty and thereafter fails to appear before the Inquiring Authority without sufficient cause, the Inquiring Authority may:

options.A: Drop the charges altogether
options.B: Postpone the inquiry indefinitely
options.C: Hold the inquiry ex parte
options.D: Impose the penalty without holding any inquiry

e: Where the charged railway servant does not plead guilty and thereafter fails to appear before the Inquiring Authority without sufficient cause, the Inquiring Authority may hold the inquiry ex parte.

q: Where the appellate authority proposes to enhance the penalty imposed on a railway servant, it shall:

options.A: Enhance the penalty without any notice, as the appeal is the employee's own remedy
options.B: Give the appellant a reasonable opportunity of making a representation against the proposed enhancement
options.C: Remand the case for a fresh inquiry in every case
options.D: Obtain the prior approval of the Railway Board in every case

e: Where the appellate authority proposes to enhance the penalty, it must give the appellant a reasonable opportunity of making a representation against the proposed enhancement before doing so.

q: Against an order passed by the appellate authority under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules:

options.A: A second appeal lies to the next higher authority
options.B: A fresh appeal lies to the President of India
options.C: The charged servant may appeal to the Central Administrative Tribunal only after ten years
options.D: No further appeal is provided for; only revision or review by the competent authority, as per the rules, is possible

e: The Discipline and Appeal Rules provide no further appeal against an order of the appellate authority; the only remedies available are revision or review by the competent authority as per the rules.

q: Premature retirement of a railway servant in public interest on completion of the prescribed qualifying service, ordered under the relevant retirement rules:

options.A: Is not a penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.B: Is a major penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.C: Is a minor penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.D: Has the same effect as dismissal from service

e: Premature retirement of a railway servant in public interest on completion of the prescribed qualifying service is ordered under the retirement rules and is not a penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: The Inquiring Authority in a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules may be:

options.A: Only the disciplinary authority himself
options.B: Only an officer of the Vigilance Department
options.C: Any serving or retired railway servant appointed for the purpose by the disciplinary authority
options.D: Only a judicial officer

e: The Inquiring Authority under the Discipline and Appeal Rules may be any serving or retired railway servant appointed for the purpose by the disciplinary authority; it need not be the disciplinary authority himself.

q: An appeal against an order of suspension under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules lies to:

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The authority to which the authority which made the suspension order is immediately subordinate
options.C: The Railway Board in all cases
options.D: The Central Administrative Tribunal directly

e: An appeal against an order of suspension lies to the authority to which the authority which made the suspension order is immediately subordinate.

q: 'Cadre check', as exercised in the Accounts Office, is distinct from 'scale check' in that cadre check verifies:

options.A: The arithmetical accuracy of the pay bills
options.B: Whether the pay drawn by each employee is in the correct level
options.C: The correctness of the sanction to the post
options.D: The distribution of the staff borne in the different grades of a cadre against the sanctioned strength of each grade

e: Cadre check verifies the distribution of the staff borne in the different grades of a cadre against the sanctioned strength of each grade, whereas scale check verifies the correctness of the pay level drawn.

q: The 'Book of Sanctions' maintained in a railway office is the record in which are entered:

options.A: All sanctions relating to the creation, extension or continuance of posts and other establishment sanctions
options.B: All punishments awarded to staff
options.C: The names of staff sanctioned leave
options.D: Sanctions for purchase of stores only

e: The 'Book of Sanctions' is the record in which all sanctions relating to the creation, extension or continuance of posts and other establishment sanctions are entered.

q: A railway servant transferred at his own request to a post in a different seniority unit is assigned seniority in the new unit:

options.A: With reference to his original date of appointment
options.B: Below all the existing staff of that seniority unit, i.e., at the bottom
options.C: Above all the existing staff of that unit
options.D: In the middle of the seniority list of the unit

e: A railway servant transferred at his own request to a post in a different seniority unit is assigned seniority at the bottom, below all the existing staff of that unit.

q: Appointments on compassionate grounds on the Railways are restricted to:

options.A: 10% of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota
options.B: 25% of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota
options.C: 5% of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota
options.D: There is no ceiling on such appointments

e: Appointments on compassionate grounds on the Railways are restricted to 5% of the vacancies falling in the direct recruitment quota.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A temporary post is a post sanctioned for a limited period carrying a definite rate of pay sanctioned for that period.
2. The cadre of a service is periodically restructured on the basis of functional justification, work studies and yardsticks.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a temporary post is one sanctioned for a limited period at a definite rate of pay, and cadres are periodically restructured on the basis of functional justification, work studies and yardsticks.

q: Which of the following advances admissible to a railway servant is interest-free?

options.A: House Building Advance
options.B: Personal Computer Advance
options.C: Advance for purchase of a motor car
options.D: Festival Advance

e: Of the advances listed, the Festival Advance is interest-free, whereas House Building Advance, Personal Computer Advance and motor car advance all carry interest.

q: On retirement, a railway servant settling down at his home town or other selected place is entitled to:

options.A: Travelling Allowance for the journey of himself and his family from the last station of duty to the place of settlement
options.B: Only Composite Transfer Grant, without any Travelling Allowance
options.C: Travelling Allowance only for himself and not for his family
options.D: Neither Travelling Allowance nor Composite Transfer Grant

e: On retirement, a railway servant settling at his home town or other selected place is entitled to Travelling Allowance for the journey of himself and his family from the last station of duty to the place of settlement.

q: The advance admissible to a railway servant in connection with Leave Travel Concession is limited to:

options.A: 50% of the estimated cost of the journey
options.B: 90% of the estimated cost of the journey
options.C: 75% of the estimated cost of the journey
options.D: The full estimated cost of the journey

e: The advance admissible to a railway servant in connection with Leave Travel Concession is limited to 90% of the estimated cost of the journey.
